label: Droplet flames: how they ended
definition: A burning fuel droplet in a chamber of known gas. 'Went out by itself' = PSI's 'Extinction'. 'Burned until the test ended' = 'Completion' (fuel used up) or 'Disruption' (the droplet was disturbed while burning). Both are counted together and the three are shown separately in each cell.

skill.gate: Estimates are shown only if cross-validated accuracy beats always guessing the commoner outcome by 5% and AUC is at least 0.70.
skill.reason: Accuracy 78% against 68% for always guessing the commoner outcome, AUC 0.80: the model beats guessing, so estimates are shown for untested cells inside the tested range.

patterns.text: At 0.34 oxygen or more, the outcome was "burned until the test ended" in all 9 tests and "went out by itself" in none.
At 0.15 oxygen or less, the outcome was "went out by itself" in 45 of 48 tests.

Tests with the outcome "went out by itself", by what else was in the chamber gas: carbon dioxide: 87 of 122; helium: 40 of 50; nitrogen only: 58 of 101. This compares observed counts only; the tests did not vary one gas at a time.

0 of 273 usable tests lie inside the selected habitat's oxygen and pressure box. 23 more lie within 0.05 oxygen and 2 psi of it (their pressures run 10.3 to 10.5 psi); the outcome was "burned until the test ended" in 23 of those.
